Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This call is being recorded for claim purposes. Can you
confirm you're comfortable continuing?
A: Yes, that's fine.
Q: Can you describe where you were when the collision happened?
A: I was stopped at a traffic light in Houston, Texas, in the right lane of a main road. Traffic had slowed down ahead of
me.
Q: What happened next?
A: The car behind me didn't stop in time. I felt a hard jolt from the back, and my head snapped forward and then back
against the headrest.
Q: Did you get out of your vehicle at the scene?
A: I got out briefly, but my neck was already stiff and I felt dizzy, so I sat back down until the police arrived.
Q: Did the other driver say anything about what happened?
A: They apologized and said they had looked down at their phone for a second. They didn't seem hurt.
Q: Did you seek medical attention?
A: Yes, I was taken to an urgent care clinic that evening. They did X-rays and told me I had soft tissue injuries
consistent with whiplash.
Q: What symptoms are you still experiencing?
A: I have neck pain, stiffness when I turn my head, and headaches most afternoons. Sitting at a desk for long periods
makes it worse.
Q: Have you started any treatment since then?
A: I'm seeing a physical therapist twice a week, and my doctor has me on anti-inflammatory medication.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add?
A: Just that I want to get back to normal as soon as possible. I'm willing to provide my medical records.
Q: Thank you. We'll follow up with you in writing. Have a good day.
A: Thank you, you too.
</page>
